    Ray categories #

    Ray categories after Gabriel–Roiter, Section 13.4 (recalled in Bongartz, Indecomposables live in all smaller lengths, Section 2.1). A ray category is a category P with zero morphisms such that

    1. objects are pairwise non-isomorphic (P is skeletal);
    2. composition with a zero morphism is zero;
    3. for each x, P(x, y) = {0} = P(y, x) for almost all y;
    4. each P(x, x) is {1, σ, …, σ^{n-1}} with σ^n = 0 ≠ σ^{n-1};
    5. each P(x, y) is cyclic under P(x, x) or under P(y, y);
    6. λ ≫ μ ≫ κ = λ ≫ ν ≫ κ ≠ 0 implies μ = ν.

    The class IsRayCategory records the consequences of these axioms used in this development (skeletal, locally finite, finite hom sets, nonzero identities, nilpotent non-identity endomorphisms); the BGRS ray category of a distributive algebra satisfies them (RayCategories/Distributive/FromDistributive.lean).

      class LargeIndecomposable.IsRayCategory (P : Type u) [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} P] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms P] :
      Prop

      The axioms of a finite-type ray category used here: skeletal, locally finite (axiom 3), finite hom sets with nonzero identities, and nilpotent non-identity endomorphisms (consequences of axioms 4 and 5). Gabriel–Roiter's cyclicity and cancellation axioms are not needed for the results below.

      • skeletal : CategoryTheory.Skeletal P
      • finite_out (x : P) : {y : P | ∃ (f : x ⟶ y), f ≠ 0}.Finite

        Axiom 3: an object is linked by nonzero morphisms to finitely many objects.

      • finite_in (x : P) : {y : P | ∃ (f : y ⟶ x), f ≠ 0}.Finite
      • finite_hom (x y : P) : Finite (x ⟶ y)
      • id_ne_zero (x : P) : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id x ≠ 0
      • nil (x : P) (e : x ⟶ x) : e ≠ CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id x → ∃ (n : ℕ), rpow e n = 0

        Non-identity endomorphisms are nilpotent.
